entries.title: M/s V.H. Patel & Company v. Hirubhai Himabhai Patel
entries.summary: The dispute arose among partners under a broad reference covering partnership disputes. The Supreme Court held that dissolution of the partnership could be decided in arbitration where the reference encompassed that dispute and remitted the dissolution claim for arbitral consideration.
entries.holding: A dispute concerning dissolution of a partnership may be decided by an arbitrator when it falls within the arbitration reference; dissolution is not reserved exclusively for court determination.
keyParagraphs: The partners' disputes, including the claim for dissolution of the partnership firm, had been referred to arbitration under a broad consent reference.
The Court concluded that the dissolution claim was within the arbitrator's jurisdiction and required arbitral consideration.

entries.title: Jagdish Chander v. Ramesh Chander
entries.summary: A partnership deed stated that disputes would be referred to arbitration only if the parties later so determined. The Supreme Court held that this conditional language was not a binding arbitration agreement under Section 7 and set aside the arbitrator's appointment.
entries.holding: A clause requiring a future mutual decision to arbitrate lacks the present consensus ad idem required by Section 7 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
keyParagraphs: Clause 16 provided that a partnership dispute would be referred for arbitration if the parties so determined.
Because a fresh consensus was required after the dispute arose, the clause was not an arbitration agreement under Section 7; the Section 11 appointment was set aside.

entries.title: Purushottam s/o Tulsiram Badwaik v. Anil
entries.summary: A partnership agreement made after the 1996 Act referred disputes to arbitration under the repealed 1940 Act. The Supreme Court held that the mistaken statutory reference did not invalidate the parties' binding agreement and directed application of the 1996 Act.
entries.holding: Where the agreement satisfies Section 7 and proceedings did not commence under the 1940 Act, an obsolete reference to the 1940 Act does not defeat the parties' binding intention to arbitrate under the 1996 Act.
keyParagraphs: Clause 15 required disputes connected with the partnership business to be referred to arbitration and made the decision final and binding.
The reference to the repealed 1940 Act was of no consequence; the binding arbitration agreement was governed by the 1996 Act.
